predeclared_metrics.quality_rule: An arm replaces C0 as the production generation model only if (1) the paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20260926) 95% lower bound of micro-F1(arm) - micro-F1(C0) is at least -0.02, (2) its median decode tokens/s exceeds C0's, (3) its JSON-valid rate is at least 0.98, and (4) it had no memory or deadline failure. Inference speed alone does not pass. C1 or C2 passing means keep the model and change only the serving profile. Micro-F1 is over per-accession item-code sets against the filer-declared header ITEMS; macro-F1, exact match and per-filing precision and recall are reported alongside.
predeclared_metrics.usage_rule: Retain llama-server usage (prompt and completion tokens) and timings per filing as local-model counters. No provider usage, cache categories or token-savings claim; unknown values stay null.

failures_and_skips.reason: acquire.py refused with state_dir_must_be_owner_only before any SEC request: the existing state directory was not owner-only. The refusal comes before the run directory is created. The coordinator set the directory to 0700 and reran the same run id (li26-acq-attempt-2). The exit status was not retained.

window.sh's admission check refused C2 before any load: 17,366 MiB were free against the 17,535 required. Production had been idle-sleeping (--sleep-idle-seconds 600) with about 438 MiB loaded, so stopping it freed far less than the 9,478 MiB that the window's start prediction adds. Nothing started. C2 ran in window w-20260926T102638Z (li26-c2-w3) after further Windows-side applications were closed.

Failed frozen criterion (1): the paired bootstrap 95% lower bound of micro-F1(M) - micro-F1(C0) is -0.0560, below the -0.02 margin (point -0.0240, upper -0.0049); micro-F1 was 0.9670 against 0.9909. Criteria (2) to (4) held: median decode 80.16 against 5.25 tokens/s, JSON-valid 1.0, and failure-free. The outcome is retain_control.

limitations: Native execution on nativestack-5975wx-20260925, one run per arm, under the frozen protocol. No arm was repeated, so run-to-run variance is unmeasured. Speed and memory are this host's, under its load at the time: a shared WSL2 desktop with the Windows-side GPU applications closed for each window. They are not isolated benchmarks.
Labels are filer-declared header ITEMS, not hand-checked or frontier-model labels; the task is a proxy for catalyst extraction and does not meet that catalog trial's gate.
One day of filings (360 accessions, all eligible, from 2020-03-02); not a representative sample of 8-K forms or years.
Inputs are capped at 16,000 characters (head and tail; 11 of 360 were cut); items in a dropped middle are unreachable for every arm alike.

The three windows ran at different times on 2026-09-26 on a shared WSL2 desktop, so timing and memory are shared-host, whole-device observations. C0 finished in one segment rather than the expected two.

Admission needed the Windows-side GPU applications closed first. Window 1's closes went by image name, with a forced second pass, not by the PIDs that README step 3 names. Window 3 followed further closes outside that list, under the user approval the coordinator recorded. C2 was refused once (window 2) before it was admitted in window 3.
C1 and C2 differ from the tasked profiles (-ngl 99 without FFN offload; the MTP draft file), which cannot be admitted beside the embeddings service on this host; those profiles have no result.

Device-memory estimates are planning figures from the GGUF tensor table and a fixed overhead, and the production estimate overstates what stopping an idle-sleeping production unit frees; the measured guard protected other GPU users.
B and X are excluded by pinned-runtime evidence, not by a load attempt; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is excluded by size.
Greedy non-thinking decoding is a fixed protocol, not each publisher's recommended setting.

C1 and C2 predicted the same item sets as C0 on all 360 filings, so their bootstrap interval is exactly zero. MTP accepted 4,735 of 4,737 drafted tokens on replies averaging about 17 tokens. C2's decode gain is established for this protocol only, not for production's own sampled or thinking requests.

Production now runs C2 with no free-memory guard of its own. C2's minimum whole-device free memory was 3,829 MiB with the Windows-side applications closed, so Windows-side GPU applications reopened later can exhaust device memory.
The production switch and its immediate checks come from the coordinator's dated operations log. A later read-only recheck is recorded in two llama-cpp host receipts that carry self reviews only.

rollback: Production changed only because the frozen rule passed. It now runs C2 through the systemd --user drop-in nativestack-generation.service.d/li26-c2-serving-profile.conf, which resets ExecStart with four changed options (--gpu-layers 36 -> 99, plus --n-cpu-ffn 20, --spec-type draft-mtp and --spec-draft-n-max 3). Rollback removes that drop-in, runs systemctl --user daemon-reload, restarts nativestack-generation.service and checks /health 200. The base unit (C0's serving profile, 36 GPU layers) and the model file are unchanged, so rollback restores the pre-switch production unit. Each window's own stop was undone by its exit trap: restore timers were cancelled and /health was ok.
next_decision_changing_test: Measure C2 on production's own requests (sampled and thinking, longer replies): decode speed, MTP acceptance, and free device memory with the Windows-side applications back in use. Reopen if free memory approaches the 3,072 MiB reserve, production shows allocation failures, or quality regresses. A repeated run of the frozen task would bound run-to-run variance. B or X re-enter only under a new plan with a pinned runtime that supports them.
